title: TIER: Threat Implicitness Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety Behaviors
abstract: arXiv:2609.05117v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Current LLM safety benchmarks largely rely on binary metrics, overlooking how models respond to harmful prompts with varying threat implicitness. We introduce TIER, a Threat Implicitness Benchmark for behavioral safety evaluation of LLMs. TIER covers four risk domains and four threat levels, from explicit harmful requests to sophisticated jailbreaks. Responses are assessed using a six-label behavior scale and two independent LLM judges. Experiments on six open-weight LLMs show that safety behaviors evolve gradually across threat levels rather than shifting directly from refusal to compliance. Contextual prompts yield the most diverse behaviors, while jailbreaks reveal the largest robustness gaps. Furthermore, models with similar Attack Success Rates can exhibit distinct response distributions, highlighting the need for behavior-aware LLM safety evaluation.

translated_title: TIER：用于评估大语言模型安全行为的威胁隐含性基准
translated_abstract: 当前的大语言模型安全基准主要依赖二元指标，忽视了模型对具有不同威胁隐含程度的有害提示的响应方式。我们提出了TIER，一个用于大语言模型行为安全评估的威胁隐含性基准。TIER涵盖四个风险领域和四个威胁等级，从明确的有害请求到复杂的越狱攻击。模型响应通过六类行为量表和两个独立的大语言模型评判器进行评估。在六个开源权重大语言模型上的实验表明，安全行为随威胁等级逐渐演变，而非直接从拒绝转变为服从。情境化提示产生最多样的行为，而越狱攻击则暴露出最大的鲁棒性差距。此外，攻击成功率相似的模型可能表现出截然不同的响应分布，这凸显了基于行为视角进行大语言模型安全评估的必要性。
tldr: 提出TIER威胁隐含性基准，通过四个风险领域、四个威胁等级和六类行为量表评估大语言模型安全，发现模型安全行为随威胁隐含程度逐渐演变而非简单在拒绝与服从间切换，且攻击成功率相似的模型可能呈现截然不同的响应分布。
en_tdlr: TIER, a threat implicitness benchmark covering four risk domains and four threat levels, reveals that LLM safety behaviors evolve gradually across threat levels rather than shifting directly from refusal to compliance, and models with similar attack success rates can exhibit distinct response distributions.
